source.title: SAEs Can Improve Unlearning: Dynamic Sparse Autoencoder Guardrails for Precision Unlearning in LLMs
source.authors: Aashiq Muhamed; Jacopo Bonato; Mona T. Diab; Virginia Smith

record.tranche_reason: The study tests fine-tuning recovery after RMU unlearning and reports that recovery depends on whether DSG guardrails are applied. It refines the claim by showing recovery for RMU alone but resistance or delayed recovery with DSG, under the tested attack settings.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study’s WMDP-Bio fine-tuning relearning experiments and the WMDP unlearning accuracies relevant to whether DSG reduces targeted performance while retaining utility. The study does not test recovery by ablation, quantization, or prompting. Values visible only in plotted curves are recorded as figure only; textual descriptions are used for their states.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own fine-tuning relearning attacks on gemma-2-2b-it. It shows RMU recovers at lr 1e-5 but not at 1e-6, and that its new activation-based method (DSG) resists or delays recovery. These results bear on B (RMU) and F (DSG). Its WMDP accuracy-plus-MMLU results bear on the first half of A. None of the original sources is this paper.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Additions: the authors frame DSG's robustness for an API (black-box) threat model and exclude white-box obfuscation attacks. They note that relearning efficacy depends strongly on learning rate, and they suggest learning-rate limits as an added defense.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates Dynamic SAE Guardrails, which conditionally clamp selected SAE features, and compares against RMU followed by fine-tuning on WMDP-Bio. It does not reproduce the original WMDP, Who’s Harry Potter, or Eight Methods protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning outcomes vary with defense configuration and learning rate: test-time versus train-time DSG, their combination, and learning rate 1e-5 versus 1e-6 change the reported recovery pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning leaves activation geometry nearly unchanged (mean cosine 0.994, magnitude ratio 1.020). With train-time DSG, WMDP-Bio training loss stays much higher than MMLU loss (Fig 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning changes weights but barely changes activation directions, so activation-space interventions persist under relearning.

record.problems: The relearning curves are primarily reported in figures without exact values for most epochs. The attack is tested on WMDP-Bio only and uses the WMDP-Bio test set; the study does not report recovery from a small unrelated or loosely related set. The reduced-learning-rate results are described as minimal changes, without exact curve values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for MMLU utility curves during relearning were retained; the text describes comparable MMLU performance for base fine-tuning with and without test-time DSG and moderate utility decline for train-time DSG at higher epochs, but the plotted values are not stated. Other unlearning benchmark results not directly about relearning recovery are omitted.

untested.parts: Recovery by quantization, prompting or activation ablation for any method; models other than gemma-2-2b-it; unfiltered WMDP question sets.

Small, unrelated or loosely related relearning sets, or a held-out subset of the forgotten facts. Relearning is only on the WMDP-Bio test set itself, only for RMU and DSG, only on one 2B model, with no Cyber relearning.
Not tested. DSG blocks access by design, but there is no analysis of whether other methods delete or hide knowledge.
Not tested. This matters for DSG because it relies on an input classifier that rephrasing could evade.

DSG is tested only against fine-tuning on one 2B model. Not tested against prompting, rephrasing, jailbreaks, quantization, or white-box/obfuscation attacks, which the authors set aside via an API threat model.

record.verdict_notes: Reader version codes V1, V2 and V6 were mapped to A, B and F. DSG is an inference-time gating guardrail that leaves knowledge in the weights; the paper itself calls it blocking pathways. Its F robustness is therefore about access control, and prompt-level attacks on its classifier are untested. Figure 5 values and the question set used for relearning evaluation are not given in text; the y-axis spans roughly 0.2 to 0.7, while target accuracy on the filtered set is 100%, so the relearning evaluation may use a different question set. MUSE results (e.g. RMU KnowMem reduction 9.8%/3.9% vs DSG 98.5%/94.7%) bear on A but are declared as left out.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests WMDP unlearning and fine-tuning attacks on WMDP-Bio configurations, but does not test the full range of unlearning methods or attack types in the claim.
The attack fine-tunes on the WMDP-Bio test set for 10 epochs; small-set size and recovery from unrelated, loosely related, or merely partial forgotten facts are not stated or tested.
Ablating an activation direction to restore knowledge is not tested. The paper describes activation clamping as blocking pathways, but does not test whether knowledge was deleted versus inaccessible.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context recovery are not tested.
DSG is tested against fine-tuning relearning only, not against ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks.

relation.reason: Its own relearning runs on RMU and DSG bear on versions B and F, and its WMDP/MMLU results bear on A.

tranche.reason: Its results qualify versions: recovery depends on learning rate (B), RMU stays short of chance under the utility rule (A), test-time DSG alone erodes (F). T2 is also arguable.

source_check.notes: R1-R4 baselines: target model scores 100% on permutation-filtered questions (522/1273 Bio, 275/1987 Cyber; chance 25%), so not comparable to raw-WMDP numbers. The relearning attack fine-tunes on the WMDP-Bio test set itself. DSG robustness is framed for an API threat model and excludes white-box obfuscation attacks. Per App I.5, the Sec 4.3 RMU is the Sec 4.1 Bio config.

statements.correction: DSG, gemma-2-2b-it (2B), permutation-filtered WMDP (target 100%, chance 25%): Bio 29.64 with MMLU 99.34; Cyber 26.74 with MMLU 99.73. The Bio config was attacked by relearning (Sec 4.3): test-time DSG alone rises gradually at lr 1e-5 (figure only).
statements.problem: Cites R1 and R2 but never gives DSG's result. Two of its conditions are wrong for this study: '6–70B' and 'No recovery attack on these checkpoints'.

statements.correction: RMU, gemma-2-2b-it, filtered WMDP (target 100%): Bio 50.00, Cyber 88.00. Config chosen to minimise WMDP with MMLU at least 99% of target.
statements.problem: Does not name this study. R3 and R4 are a single RMU config under a 99%-MMLU rule, with no within-study contrast of layer, retain set or selection rule.

statements.correction: gemma-2-2b-it RMU, fine-tuned 10 epochs on the WMDP-Bio test set: at lr 1e-6, all configurations show minimal change (Fig 10, figure only). At lr 1e-5, RMU rises rapidly and exceeds the fine-tuned base (R7).
statements.problem: At lr 1e-6 the study reports minimal change, i.e. no recovery, not partial recovery. Cited R7 shows rapid recovery at lr 1e-5, which does not fit 'recover only partly'. 'DSG RMU' means RMU alone in this study.

statements.correction: R8: gemma-2-2b-it with RMU weights plus test-time DSG, fine-tuned 10 epochs at lr 1e-5 on the WMDP-Bio test set (in-domain), stays near-random (25%) throughout. This is the DSG authors' own test.
statements.problem: Cites R8, but its conditions (listed models; 'benign, unrelated or out-of-domain' fine-tuning) do not fit this study's attack or model.

statements.correction: gemma-2-2b-it, lr 1e-5, 10 epochs on the WMDP-Bio test set (figure only): RMU+test-time DSG near 25% throughout; Base+test-time DSG rises gradually; train-time DSG holds random for about 6 epochs, then recovers; both combined hold through epoch 7.
statements.problem: Files this study under 'challenges', but R6, R9 and R10 show partial or delayed resistance (limits_scope, l5). '3B-8B LLMs' also excludes this 2B model.

statements.correction: Train-time DSG (gemma-2-2b-it, lr 1e-5, WMDP-Bio test set): random-level for about 6 of 10 epochs, then gradual recovery. WMDP-Bio accuracy, figure only.
statements.problem: Does not name this study, but R9 fits the point (recovery delayed, not prevented).

statements.correction: Train-time DSG (gemma-2-2b-it, lr 1e-5): random-level for about 6 epochs, then gradual recovery (figure only).
statements.problem: Does not name this study. R9 fits the epochs dose factor: resistance lasts about 6 epochs, then recovery.

statements.correction: At lr 1e-5, RMU recovers and Base+test-time DSG rises gradually. At lr 1e-6, all configurations change minimally (Fig 10). RMU+test-time DSG is flat at both rates.
statements.problem: The study does show that the attack's learning rate matters, but cited R12 (RMU+test-time DSG, lr 1e-6) shows no contrast: it is flat at both lr 1e-5 (R8) and lr 1e-6.
